bug_description.normalized: The saved ASan trace and the staged vulnerable checkout both match pre-`139c94fc8f8cf509f5dae3108b86a596d52a2276` source lines 693/1200/1650/1679 in `src/lib/lwan-request.c`, so this GT is grounded in the reproducing staged revision `341dca6b2594eea98df73dcdb96bb80b6ccc9fb9` rather than the later sample-metadata commit `139c94fc8f8cf509f5dae3108b86a596d52a2276`, which already adds `data_copy[length - 1] = '\0';`. In that staged revision, the 32773-byte witness reaches `fuzz_parse_http_request()`, which truncates `length` to the 32767-byte global `data_copy` buffer and copies only the first 32767 bytes. That copied prefix starts with a PROXY v2 LOCAL header whose length field is `0x0020`, so `parse_proxy_protocol_v2()` accepts it and returns `buffer = data_copy + 48`. Direct inspection of the copied prefix shows every byte from offset 48 through 32766 is whitespace (`0x20`, `0x0d`, or `0x0a`) under `lwan_char_isspace()`. `parse_http_request()` then calls `ignore_leading_whitespace(buffer)` without checking that any non-whitespace byte or full request remains inside `helper->buffer->len`. Because this staged revision does not NUL-terminate `data_copy` before `parse_http_request()`, the copied buffer stays full and `ignore_leading_whitespace()` advances through all 32719 remaining bytes; the next loop test reads `*buffer` at `data_copy + 32767`, the first byte past the array. AddressSanitizer reports `global-buffer-overflow READ 1` in `ignore_leading_whitespace`; the later fix commit expresses the missing obligation by introducing `min_request_size` checks around this whitespace-skipping point, but Stage 02 did not dynamically validate the fixed image.

source.description: First parser statement that materializes the post-proxy request pointer later consumed by the unsafe whitespace skip. For the staged witness, the PROXY v2 header is accepted and this assignment updates `buffer` from `data_copy` to `data_copy + 48`.
source.value_from: The staged file `gt_results/arvo_14582/poc` is exactly 32773 bytes (sha256 `fc3e15505d6796231c1a186886df20f9c452f4d6f3de4a0bc4b956bf387addfe`). `fuzz_parse_http_request()` truncates it to the first 32767 bytes before parsing. In that copied prefix, bytes 0..11 are the PROXY v2 signature `0d0a0d0a000d0a515549540a`, bytes 12..15 are `20 20 00 20` so `cmd_ver == 0x20` (`LOCAL`) and `hdr->len == 0x0020`, and every copied byte from offset 48 through 32766 is whitespace (`0x20`, `0x0d`, or `0x0a`).

sink.description: ASan crash site. After the loop body has advanced `buffer` to `data_copy + 32767`, the next loop test dereferences `*buffer` at the first byte past the 32767-byte global `data_copy` array, just beyond the last valid element `data_copy[32766]`.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow ... READ of size 1` in `ignore_leading_whitespace /src/lwan/src/lib/lwan-request.c:693:30` and names `data_copy` at line 1650 as the overflowed global object.

root_cause.description: `parse_http_request()` invokes `ignore_leading_whitespace()` on the post-proxy pointer without first proving that the remaining logical span contains a non-whitespace byte or a complete HTTP request before `helper->buffer->value + helper->buffer->len`.
root_cause.note: After step 3, the remaining copied suffix is 32719 bytes long and entirely whitespace. The vulnerable code performs this unbounded skip anyway; the patch introduces `min_request_size` checks around this point to reject requests that are too short or leave too little data after leading whitespace.

tainted_value_origin.description: In the staged reproducing revision `341dca6b2594eea98df73dcdb96bb80b6ccc9fb9`, the first vulnerability-relevant state is the clamped parser extent. The 32773-byte witness is truncated to `length = 32767`, so the subsequent copy fills `data_copy` completely; this revision reaches `parse_http_request()` without any later `data_copy[length - 1] = '\0';` write, leaving no in-bounds terminator for `ignore_leading_whitespace()` to stop on.

parser_admitted.description:
The copied prefix begins with `

\0
QUIT
`, so with `REQUEST_ALLOW_PROXY_REQS` set and `length = 32767 > 16`, the fuzz-only `read_request_finalizer()` special case admits the buffer as a PROXY v2 request and `fuzz_parse_http_request()` proceeds to `parse_http_request()`.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzz helper truncates the 32773-byte witness to the 32767-byte global `data_copy`, fills that array completely, and publishes the copied `(value,len)` pair to the parser.
Because proxy parsing is enabled and the copied prefix is a PROXY v2 LOCAL header with `len = 0x0020`, the parser accepts the header and moves `buffer` to `data_copy + 48`.
`parse_http_request()` immediately runs `ignore_leading_whitespace()` on that post-proxy pointer without verifying that any non-whitespace request bytes remain inside the 32767-byte logical buffer.

Every copied byte from offset 48 through 32766 is whitespace, so the loop advances to `data_copy + 32767` and the next `*buffer` test produces the saved AddressSanitizer global-buffer-overflow READ 1.

fine_trace.note: The staged witness file is 32773 bytes, so the fuzz helper clamps `length` to `sizeof(data_copy) == 32767` before parsing. This singular truncation makes the later copy fill the global array completely in the reproducing staged revision `341dca6b2594eea98df73dcdb96bb80b6ccc9fb9`.

Copies only the first 32767 bytes of the witness into static global `data_copy`. Because `length` now equals the array size, every byte of `data_copy[0..32766]` is attacker-controlled and, in this pre-`139c94fc` staged revision, no subsequent statement NUL-terminates `data_copy` before `parse_http_request()` runs.

Publishes the copied bytes to the request parser as the logical span `[data_copy, data_copy + 32767)`. All later bounds decisions, including the unsafe whitespace skip, use this full `(value,len)` pair.

Source. Proxy parsing is enabled in the fuzz helper, and the copied prefix begins with the PROXY v2 signature `

\0
QUIT
`. `parse_proxy_protocol_v2()` therefore interprets bytes 14..15 as `hdr->len == 0x0020`, computes a 48-byte header, accepts the `LOCAL` command byte `0x20`, and returns `buffer = data_copy + 48` because `48 < helper->buffer->len` in the staged 32767-byte logical buffer.

Root cause. The returned pointer from step 3 starts at offset 48, and direct inspection of the copied prefix shows every byte from 48 through 32766 is whitespace (`0x20`, `0x0d`, or `0x0a`). In this staged revision the parser still calls the extentless whitespace skipper with no check that a non-whitespace byte or a full request remains before `helper->buffer->value + helper->buffer->len`.

With the all-whitespace post-proxy suffix from step 4, the loop body executes once for each copied byte from offsets 48..32766. After 32719 increments, `buffer` becomes `data_copy + 32767`, the first out-of-bounds byte just past the published logical span and last valid element `data_copy[32766]` in the staged revision that left the buffer unterminated.

Sink. The next loop test dereferences `*buffer` when `buffer == data_copy + 32767`, so it performs a 1-byte read at the first byte past global `data_copy`, immediately beyond the last valid element `data_copy[32766]`. This matches the saved ASan `global-buffer-overflow READ 1` at line 693 with `parse_http_request` and `fuzz_parse_http_request` immediately below it in the stack.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the invalid read is 0 bytes to the right of global variable `data_copy` defined here with size 32767.

format.name: PROXY v2 LOCAL header followed only by whitespace in the truncated copied prefix
format.contract: Exactly the 32773-byte witness stored in `gt_results/arvo_14582/poc` (sha256 `fc3e15505d6796231c1a186886df20f9c452f4d6f3de4a0bc4b956bf387addfe`). `fuzz_parse_http_request()` truncates it to the first 32767 bytes before parsing. In that copied prefix, bytes 0..11 are the PROXY v2 signature `0d0a0d0a000d0a515549540a`, bytes 12..15 are `20 20 00 20` so the parser takes the `LOCAL` command and `hdr->len == 0x0020`, and every copied byte from offset 48 through 32766 is whitespace (`0x20`, `0x0d`, or `0x0a`). Those exact witness properties make the parser advance `buffer` to `data_copy + 48` and leave `ignore_leading_whitespace()` scanning the entire remaining logical extent until the next loop test reads at `data_copy + 32767`, the first byte past the array and past the last valid element `data_copy[32766]`.
